question.prompt: Doug and Dave shared a pizza with \(8\) equally-sized slices. Doug wanted a plain pizza, but Dave wanted anchovies on half of the pizza. The cost of a plain pizza was \(\$8,\) and there was an additional cost of \(\$2\) for putting anchovies on one half. Dave ate all the slices of anchovy pizza and one plain slice. Doug ate the remainder. Each then paid for what he had eaten. How many more dollars did Dave pay than Doug?

solutions.explanation:
Separate the plain pizza cost from the anchovy charge. Each slice accounts for \(8\div8=1\) dollar of the plain pizza cost.

Half of the eight slices have anchovies, so Dave ate four anchovy slices and one plain slice, or five slices altogether. He also ate all the anchovies, so he pays the entire \(\$2\) topping charge. Dave therefore pays \(5+2=7\) dollars. Doug ate the remaining three plain slices and pays \(3\) dollars.

The difference is \(7-3=\boxed{4}\) dollars, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Price the plain slices and the topping
